messages.content:
You are an engineering drafter producing SVG drawings.

Draw the following as a single, self-contained SVG document:

Ideal (potential) flow of a uniform stream of speed U = 1 m/s in the +x direction past a circular cylinder of radius a = 0.25 m centred at the origin, in an unbounded domain. The stream function is psi = U y (1 - a^2 / r^2). Draw the cylinder and the streamlines psi = -0.8, -0.6, -0.4, -0.2, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 m^2/s inside the frame -5/3 <= x <= 5/3, -5/3 <= y <= 5/3. Streamlines may not cross the cylinder surface. Use viewBox="0 0 1000 1000". Map physical coordinates to drawing coordinates as X = 500 + 300 x and Y = 500 - 300 y. Wrap every contour in one <g data-field="psi" data-status="..."> group and set data-status honestly to one of solved, estimated, illustrative or ill-posed. Draw every contour as its own <path> or <polyline> carrying a data-level attribute with its numeric level and label it. Contours must satisfy the boundary conditions exactly.

Requirements:
- Output ONLY the SVG document. No markdown fences, no prose before or after.
- The root <svg> must declare xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" and a viewBox.
- Use only built-in SVG elements (path, line, rect, circle, ellipse, polygon,
  polyline, text, g, defs, marker, pattern). No external images, scripts,
  fonts, or stylesheets.
- Every visible element must be stroked or filled with an explicit color.
- Label parts and dimensions with <text>; keep text inside the viewBox.
- Prefer clean, precise geometry over decoration.
